metaTitle: Closed World, Open World: What the Database Assumes
excerpt: SQL treats absence as fact. A knowledge graph treats it as uncertainty. When two systems built on different world assumptions meet at a join, a federated query, or an AI agent's tool call, one of them is wrong about what silence means. The industry builds better maps. The borders remain undrawn.
metaDescription: SQL assumes absence means false. Knowledge graphs assume absence means unknown. This gap breaks data systems at every cross-source boundary.
